newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian dissident challenges Iliescu poll bid.
newsitem.headline: Romanian dissident challenges Iliescu poll bid.

text.p: Romania's best known communist-era dissident, Doina Cornea, on Friday challenged President Ion Iliescu's bid for re-election, a Central Electoral Buro (BEC) official said.

Cornea, 66, a retired academic, was one of the few dissidents who dared to speak out against the rule of late Stalinist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu. She spent two years under house arrest before Ceausescu was overthrown and executed.
The BEC said Cornea's challenge to Iliescu, a leading communist official under Ceausescu, was the sixth received since the president registered his candidacy on Thursday.
The contesters argue that Iliescu, in power since the 1989 revolt, is standing for a third term in office, which is banned by the constitution.
But Iliescu, who won elections in 1990 and 1992, says his first term pre-dates the post-communist constitution of 1991 which limits presidents to two four-year terms in office.
Cornea has long accused Iliescu of abuse of power and betraying the revolution.
The League for Human Rights (LADO) and the Civic Alliance, a small centrist political group, were first to present their challenge to Iliescu's well-funded campaign.

"In November 1996 he (Iliescu) wants another four-year mandate...in total 11 years. This is the way towards dictatorship," said the text of the challenges, which ask the BEC to admit the suit and reject the candidacy.
The BEC will send the challenge to the constitutional court which is expected to rule next week.

"If Iliescu's candidacy is accepted, we'll put the case to Strasbourg's human rights commission and the OSCE department in Warsaw supervising the elections in the former communist countries," said LADO chairman Stefanescu Draganesti.
Iliescu, who stands for the leftist Party of Social Democracy, is favourite to win the November 3 presidential ballot, which coincides with parliamentary polls.
